user.title: Oswald Conversation
user.description: Connect Home Assistant Assist to the authenticated Oswald Home Assistant WebSocket endpoint.

data_description.auth_token: Use the token configured on the Oswald server. Bearer tokens are sent without encryption over ws://; use wss:// unless the connection is on a trusted network.
data_description.default_user_id: Requests without an authenticated user, including satellite requests, will assume this user's identity. Only enable this temporary fallback if you trust every device that can access the Assist pipeline.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure Oswald Conversation
reconfigure.description: Update and verify the authenticated Oswald Home Assistant WebSocket endpoint.

data_description.auth_token: Leave the masked value unchanged or clear the field to keep an existing token. If no token is stored, enter one. Bearer tokens are sent without encryption over ws://; use wss:// unless the connection is on a trusted network.
data_description.default_user_id: Requests without an authenticated user, including satellite requests, will assume this user's identity. Only enable this temporary fallback if you trust every device that can access the Assist pipeline.

reauth_confirm.title: Authenticate Oswald Conversation
reauth_confirm.description: Enter the token configured on the Oswald server. Older entries without a token must authenticate before they can be used. If the endpoint URL has changed, reconfigure the integration instead.

data_description.auth_token: Enter a new token; blank or masked values cannot be used for reauthentication. Bearer tokens are sent without encryption over ws://; use wss:// unless the connection is on a trusted network.

error.invalid_ws_url: Enter a valid ws:// or wss:// URL without credentials or a fragment
error.invalid_auth: Enter a valid authentication token; the token is missing or was rejected
error.invalid_user: Select an active Home Assistant user
error.unsupported_protocol: The endpoint does not support Oswald Home Assistant protocol v1
